heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 Mini can successfully run Polymaker Fiberon PA612-CF15 up to a calculated safe print speed of 143 mm/s (12 mm³/s volumetric flow limit), but requires a hardened steel hotend swap to prevent immediate nozzle destruction. While PA612 exhibits lower warp tendencies than standard PA6, drafts on this open-frame printer necessitate printing inside a draft-free room or tent alongside an active dry box.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with PVP-based glue stick or dedicated nylon bed adhesive (e.g., Magigoo PA)
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 12 mm³/s in the filament profile to cap print speeds safely at 143 mm/s.
Enable Wipe While Retracting (2 mm distance) and activate retract on layer change to mitigate carbon fiber oozing.
Configure Part Cooling Fan threshold: Keep cooling at 0% for layers 1-3, ramping up to a maximum of 25% only for overhangs and short layer times under 15 seconds.
Set Wall Generator to Arachne with an outer wall speed of 80 mm/s and inner wall speed of 120 mm/s to optimize dimensional accuracy.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and rough, porous surface finish
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Wet filament; PA612-CF is hygroscopic and rapidly absorbs ambient moisture even during a few hours of open-air printing.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament in an active blast oven at 80°C for 8-12 hours and print directly from a heated dry box using PTFE tubing directly to the toolhead.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Corner lifting and print warping on parts larger than 50mm
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Differential thermal contraction accelerated by ambient drafts on the open-frame A1 Mini chassis.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a generous 5-8 mm outer brim with a 0.1 mm brim-object gap, place a draft shield around the printer, and keep part cooling off (0%).

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clicking, under-extrusion, or rapid bore enlargement
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Printing abrasive carbon fiber composite through the stock stainless steel nozzle or exceeding the 12 mm³/s flow capability.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Install an official Bambu Lab 0.4mm or 0.6mm Hardened Steel Hotend assembly and confirm volumetric flow rate is clamped at or below 12 mm³/s.

faq.question: Can I print Fiberon PA612-CF15 on the A1 Mini with the stock nozzle?
faq.answer: No. The stock A1 Mini hotend uses a stainless steel nozzle which will wear out and widen within a few hundred grams of CF filament; you must upgrade to the Bambu hardened steel hotend.

faq.question: Does the A1 Mini need a full enclosure to print PA612-CF15?
faq.answer: Not necessarily for small-to-medium parts, as PA612 has significantly lower shrinkage than PA6, but you must prevent drafts and avoid high part cooling fan speeds.

faq.question: Can I feed this filament directly from the Bambu AMS Lite?
faq.answer: No. Carbon fiber filaments are abrasive and can groove AMS Lite plastic funnels, and unsealed open spools will absorb ambient moisture rapidly; feed directly from an active dry box.

faq.question: What nozzle temperature should I set in OrcaSlicer for this material?
faq.answer: Set the nozzle temperature to 285°C for all layers (within the 275°C-295°C range), pairing it with a 50°C bed temperature to guarantee proper fusion and flow.
